description: Compute the Even-winning region of a bounded total parity game using deterministic small progress-measure lifting.

source.title: Parity Games
source.algorithm_reference_title: Small Progress Measures for Solving Parity Games
source.license: Copyright remains with the cited publishers; clean-room algorithm description only.

contract.operation: Return the complete Even-winning vertex region for a finite total directed parity game.
contract.player_encoding: Owner 0 is Even and owner 1 is Odd.
contract.parity_convention: The minimum priority occurring infinitely often determines the winner; Even wins an even minimum and Odd wins an odd minimum, following Chapter 591 and Jurdziński.
contract.algorithm: Initialize every vertex measure to (0,0,0). Repeatedly scan vertices in ascending ID and lift each to the maximum of its current measure and the owner-selected minimum/maximum successor Prog value. The finite measure coordinates are the ranks for odd priorities 1, 3, and 5; coordinate p is bounded by the number of vertices of priority p. Prog is the least domain measure whose prefix through the source priority is at least the successor measure, strictly greater for odd source priorities, or TOP when no finite measure qualifies. Stop after a complete unchanged scan; a vertex is Even-winning iff its final measure is not TOP.
contract.tie_rule: Vertices are lifted in ascending ID during repeated full sweeps. Even vertices select the lexicographically smallest successor Prog value; Odd vertices select the largest. The fixed point is independent of the fair update order.
contract.output_encoding: One signed 64-bit integer with bit v set exactly when vertex v belongs to Even's winning region; the Odd region is the complement among vertices 0..N-1.
contract.strategy_output: Winning strategies are excluded; only the winning partition is returned.

input.edges: Directed simple arcs; duplicate arcs are rejected, self-loops are allowed, and every vertex has at least one outgoing arc.

workspace.meaning: Fixed adjacency masks, per-vertex three-rank measures, and bounded parser state for at most eight vertices and twenty arcs.
